context: Interactive Sankey diagram showing U.S. energy flow from 6 primary sources through generation types, grid infrastructure, demand sectors, to end uses — with draggable nodes and hover highlighting
first_impression: Deliberately designed with a colorblind-safe Tol muted palette, gradient links that transition between stage colors, and clear typographic hierarchy — well above generic default styling
what_works: The Tol palette (indigo → cyan → teal → sand → rose) is intentionally chosen and creates genuine color harmony across stages; gradient links blending source-to-target colors add visual sophistication, and loss flows are clearly encoded with dashed red strokes that stand out without dominating.
what_doesnt: The bottom quarter is visually congested — Generation Losses, Transmission Losses, and Distribution Losses cluster near the bottom edge with crossing dashed flows, making that region hard to parse; the sector-to-end-use flows on the right side form a dense tangle that would benefit from more vertical spread or padding.
